intro: Hervey Bay is a string of seaside suburbs on the Queensland coast, facing the sheltered water between the mainland and K'gari, where humpback whales rest on their way south. In Urangan, at its eastern end near the boat harbour, a reader photographed a fig that has grown extra trunks from its own limbs and sent it to us. It stands on private garden ground but is seen from the road.
meta_description: A fig on pillar roots beside Boat Harbour Drive in Urangan, Hervey Bay, Queensland: a reader's photograph and where to see it from the road.

trees.name: The Pillar-Root Fig of Boat Harbour Drive

location.address: Beside Boat Harbour Drive, Urangan, Hervey Bay, Queensland 4655 (seen from the road; the tree stands on the edge of a private residential village)

trees.story:
Most trees stand on one trunk. This fig in Urangan, on the eastern edge of Hervey Bay, stands on several, and a reader who walked under it sent us the photograph.

Look at the picture and count. In the middle, a knot of grey stems rises out of a mulched bed, ribbed and braided where roots have run down the bark and fused into it. To the right, a separate pillar holds up a long horizontal limb, and between them there is open daylight. That second trunk began as a thin root dropped from the branch above, which reached the soil, thickened and now carries weight. Figs that do this can go on spreading sideways for as long as they are given room, and this one has clearly been given some.

A man walking past at the edge of the frame barely reaches the first fork. We do not know which fig this is, how old it is or who planted it; the leaves are broad and glossy, as on several of the big figs of the Queensland coast. If you know, tell us here.

The tree grows on the garden edge of a private residential village beside Boat Harbour Drive. Look from the roadside near the bus stop, where the pillar roots show best in the morning light.
trees.how_to_recognise: A wide fig on a mulched garden bed: a cluster of braided grey trunks in the middle and a separate grey pillar to its right holding up a long level limb, open daylight between them.

question_meta: Where to see the pillar-root fig on Boat Harbour Drive in Urangan, Hervey Bay, Queensland: a reader's photograph and how to find it.
question_answer: The Pillar-Root Fig of Boat Harbour Drive grows in Urangan, at the eastern end of Hervey Bay in Queensland. It stands on the edge of a private residential village and is seen from Boat Harbour Drive, near the bus stop.
question_context: Urangan is the eastern end of Hervey Bay, the line of beach suburbs on the Queensland coast that looks across sheltered water to K'gari, the island long known as Fraser Island. Boat Harbour Drive runs through it towards the marina, where the whale-watching boats leave in season. Beside the road, on the garden edge of a private residential village, grows a broad fig that a reader walked under and photographed. Its crown rests on a knot of braided grey trunks and on a separate pillar that began as a root dropped from a limb above, reached the ground and thickened until it could carry weight. We do not yet know which fig it is, how old it is or who planted it; its leaves are broad and glossy like several of the big figs of the Queensland coast. The grounds are private, so look from the roadside about 30 m away. Anyone who knows this tree, its species or its age can tell us on the tree's page.

faq.q: Can I visit The Pillar-Root Fig of Boat Harbour Drive?
faq.a: You can see it from Boat Harbour Drive in Urangan, near the bus stop. The tree stands in the grounds of a private residential village, so look from the road.

faq.q: Why does the fig in Urangan have more than one trunk?
faq.a: Some figs drop roots from their limbs. When a root reaches the soil it thickens into a pillar that holds the branch up, and the tree can keep spreading.

faq.q: How old is the fig on Boat Harbour Drive?
faq.a: We do not know yet. If you know its age or who planted it, tell us on the tree's page.
